# Korean business document reference

Use this reference when the audience, source material, or requested output is
primarily Korean.

## Writing

- Use complete grammatical sentences and consistent honorific level.
- Prefer direct subject, action, owner, deadline, and evidence over nominalized
  administrative prose.
- Do not compress logic into arrows or decorative symbols.
- Keep English technical terms when they are the established working vocabulary,
  but define them on first use when the audience may not know them.
- Use one term for one concept throughout the artifact.
- Distinguish current capability, planned capability, assumption, request, and
  recommendation with explicit language.

## Dates, numbers, and names

- Use one date format consistently, such as `2026. 7. 27.` in narrative
  documents or `2026-07-27` in data-oriented material.
- State currency, unit, tax inclusion, rounding, and as-of date.
- Preserve legal entity names, department names, public-sector terminology, and
  procurement requirement numbering exactly.
- Verify Korean personal and organization names against the source instead of
  transliterating from memory.

## Typography and page behavior

- Use A4 for Korean business documents unless a template requires otherwise.
- Verify Korean glyph coverage in the selected font. Prefer an approved project
  font, Pretendard, Malgun Gothic, or another installed family with complete CJK
  support.
- Check line breaking around English terms, units, parentheses, and long
  unbroken identifiers.
- Avoid very light font weights in print and projection.
- Inspect every rendered page or slide for missing glyphs and awkward Korean
  line wraps.

## Procurement and executive material

- Preserve the buyer's headings, numbering, mandatory tables, and response order.
- Answer the requirement first, then explain.
- Make scope, exclusions, assumptions, owners, delivery evidence, auditability,
  security, on-premise constraints, and acceptance criteria explicit.
- In investor and commercial material, lead with what is sold, how money is
  made, why it repeats, and why now.

## Review

- Read the final visible content aloud once for broken syntax and ambiguous
  honorifics.
- Verify all Korean terms in charts, tables, fields, notes, and hidden review
  surfaces, not only body text.
